title: resolve-monorepo-scoping
description: Choose between two approaches: (1) discover walks the whole repo tree for every Project.toml with merged TestItemRef set, vs. (2) testaruda is invoked once per package. Document the decision in design.md with rationale. This blocks the multi-package test and the discover command.
close_reason: Decision: adopt per-package invocation (Option 2). The adapter is designed for a single package; CI invokes testaruda once per package. Rationale: aligns with Phase 1 single-package scope, testaruda's per-directory config, and Julia monorepo CI patterns. See .wai/designs/2026-07-15-monorepo-scoping.md for full analysis.

title: resolve-base-reset-coverage-spike
description: Design and run a Julia experiment to determine whether Base.reset_coverage() in Julia >=1.11 permits sequential in-process coverage counter resets for per-@testitem attribution. If yes, the ingest handler can use in-process resets instead of subprocess-per-item. If no, subprocess isolation is unconditionally necessary. Document findings in design.md and update the ingest handler approach accordingly.
close_reason: Spike complete: Base.reset_coverage() does not exist in Julia 1.12.5. No in-process coverage reset API is available at all. Coverage data is only written to .jl.cov files at process exit (post-mortem). Subprocess-per-item isolation is unconditionally necessary. See .wai/research/2026-07-15-reset-coverage-spike.md for full findings. Updated design.md and project.md to reflect confirmed findings.

title: Static-deps directionality bug — test→source edges instead of source→test
description:
## Impact

The `static-deps` command in the Python adapter records edges FROM test files TO the source files they import (test→source). Selection needs the reverse: given a changed source file, find tests that depend on it (source→test). 

## Root cause

In `adapter-python.rs`, `cmd_static_deps` does `tests_by_file.get(file)` which only returns results when the changed file IS itself a test file. If `src/cositos/model.py` is changed, `get()` returns None and no edges are created. The engine falls back to "run all tests."

## Reproduction

```bash
echo -e "\n# new function\ndef new_helper(): pass" >> src/cositos/model.py
git diff > /tmp/change.diff
testaruda select --diff /tmp/change.diff
# Expected: tests/test_model.py only
# Actual: all 119 tests (could not narrow down)
```

## Location

`adapter-python.rs` — `cmd_static_deps` function

## Action

Reverse the lookup direction: for each changed source file, find all test files that import from it. Two approaches:
1. Build full import graph at discover time (preferred — more scalable)
2. Reverse lookup at select time (lighter upfront, slower per selection)

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] When a source file is changed, `select` returns only tests that import from that source
- [ ] Python adapter creates correct source→test edges
- [ ] Existing test suite passes
- [ ] Test project (cositos) shows correct selection results

## Discovery

Found via testaruda usage report on cositos project (2026-07-14) — DRAFT-001.
acceptance_criteria: When a source file is changed, select returns only tests that import from that source. Python adapter creates correct source->test edges. Verify with: cargo test --test integration_static_deps. Existing test suite passes. Test project (cositos) shows correct selection results: testaruda select --files src/cositos/model.py --pre-edit only shows test_model.py.
notes: Spec reference: TIA-ADAPT-005 — static-deps must return candidate tests and K-valued edges for changed source files. Current implementation violates this by recording test→source instead of source→test.
close_reason: Fixed: reversed static-deps lookup direction. Changed from 'find tests at same path as changed file' to 'find test files that import from the changed source file.' 9 new tests, all 106 pass. PR a790e6c.

title: bug: adapter handshake envelope mismatch blocks all adapter communication
description: AdapterIO::spawn expects Handshake fields (name/version/protocol) at the JSON top level, but both adapter binaries wrap every response in {"ok": true, "result": {...}}. This is the only response type in the adapter protocol that omits the result wrapper. Blocks discover/static-deps/fingerprint/run-args/ingest for every configured adapter. See docs/evaluations/testaruda-evaluation.md §9.2 (I11)
acceptance_criteria: Handshake struct matches the actual wire format (enveloped like every other response)
close_reason: Handshake now deserializes through response envelope — all 88 tests pass, wire format matches real adapter output

comments.author: charly vibes
comments.text: Additional acceptance criteria: testaruda discover against a real project returns non-zero discovered test items; Integration test spawns a real adapter binary, not just in-process deserialization

title: F18: testaruda — CI should call 'just ci' instead of inlining cargo commands (single source of truth)
description:
Source: CLI consistency audit F18

Problem: testaruda's ci.yml inlines "cargo fmt -- --check", "cargo check", "cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings", "cargo test" directly in the YAML, even though testaruda's justfile has recipes that go unused by CI. This is a single-source-of-truth violation: updating the local "just" recipes does not affect what gates PRs.

Expected: Replace the inlined cargo commands with a single "just ci" invocation in ci.yml, matching wai and dont's pattern.

Files: testaruda/.github/workflows/ci.yml — replace the four cargo run steps with a single "run: just ci" step.

Reference: wai/.github/workflows/ci.yml is the canonical template.

Verification: "grep 'just ci' testaruda/.github/workflows/ci.yml" should match.

Classification: AFK (agent-friendly).

title: Graceful error when running select before init (TIA-LOCAL-006)
description:
Round 5 UX5 (blocker): Running 'testaruda select' before 'testaruda init' produces a raw SQLite error (no such table: test_items) instead of a human-actionable message.

## What was done (spec)

  - CLI SHALL verify store is initialized before any store-dependent operation
  - SHALL emit actionable error suggesting 'testaruda init'
  - Covers missing store, corrupted store, and incompatible schema version cases

## What remains (implementation)

- Catch missing .testaruda/store.db and emit friendly error
- Handle corrupted store / schema version mismatch

title: Route tracing/log output to stderr for machine-readable modes (TIA-OBS-005)
description:
Round 5 UX1 (blocker): tracing writes to stdout by default, breaking both --json and --agent machine-readable output modes. Every invocation of testaruda select --json produces a tracing INFO log line on stdout before the JSON payload, making the output unparseable by jq or any JSON consumer.

## What was done (spec)
- Added TIA-OBS-005 to openspec/specs/observability/spec.md:
  - When --json, --agent, or --pre-edit is active, all log output SHALL go to stderr
  - stdout SHALL contain only the requested machine-readable output

## What remains (implementation)
- Change tracing_subscriber::fmt() in src/main.rs to write to stderr (.with_writer(std::io::stderr))
- Also respect NO_COLOR and non-TTY coloration (UX9 — low priority, can bundle)

title: Adapter pipeline only processes changed files, never full project tree
description:
## Impact

The `select` command's `run_adapter_pipeline` iterates only over the **changed files** in the delta, not the full project tree. This means:
- The adapter is spawned only when a changed file matches its extension
- Static-deps runs only on those changed files
- Test files NOT in the change set never have their import edges recorded
- The store's dependency graph is always incomplete → selection always falls back to "run all"

## Root cause

In `main.rs`, `run_adapter_pipeline` iterates `delta.files` (the changed set) instead of the full project tree. Since static-deps only processes the files it receives, most test files never get their import dependencies recorded.

## Location
- `main.rs` — `run_adapter_pipeline` function

## Action

`run_adapter_pipeline` should also run discover + static-deps on the full project tree on first invocation (or cache results of a prior `discover` pass), not just on the changed file set.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Full project tree is processed for dependency edges at least once
- [ ] Results are cached/persisted for subsequent selections
- [ ] No unnecessary re-processing on repeated invocations
- [ ] selection works correctly on first invocation

## Discovery
Found via testaruda usage report on cositos (2026-07-14) — Section 2c.
acceptance_criteria: On first invocation, full project tree is processed before selection is computed. Subsequent invocations use cached results for unchanged files. Using testaruda select --diff on a single changed file returns only tests that import from that file (not all tests). Cargo test passes.
close_reason: Rewrote run_adapter_pipeline to walk full project tree and run discover + static-deps on ALL files, not just changed files. All 107 tests pass. PR 7f78507.

title: Adapter discover walks into .venv — 98 of 119 tests from vendored deps
description:
## Impact

The Python adapter's discover command walks `"."` with no ignore filters, picking up every `test_*.py` in `.venv/lib/python3.12/site-packages/`. On cositos, 98 out of 119 discovered tests come from vendored dependencies (jsonschema, mypy, tornado, etc.).

## Root cause

`adapter-python.rs` `cmd_discover` uses `walkdir::WalkDir::new(".")` with no exclusion patterns. The engine-level `run_discover_pipeline` in `main.rs` filters `target`, `.git`, and `node_modules`, but `.venv` is not in that list.

## Reproduction

```bash
cd /path/to/python/project
testaruda discover
# Output: "python-adapter discovered 119 test items"
# Expected: ~21 (project tests only)
```

## Location
- `adapter-python.rs` — `cmd_discover`
- `main.rs` — `run_discover_pipeline`

## Action
Add exclusion patterns: `.venv`, `venv`, `__pycache__`, `.mypy_cache`, `.pytest_cache`, `build/`, `dist/` to adapter-level discover walk, or pass ignore list from engine config.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Python adapter discover excludes `.venv` and common cache/build directories
- [ ] Only project tests are discovered
- [ ] Configurable exclusion list in `testaruda.toml`

## Discovery
Found via testaruda usage report (2026-07-14) — DRAFT-003.
acceptance_criteria: Python adapter discover excludes .venv, venv, __pycache__, .mypy_cache, .pytest_cache, build/, dist/. Only project tests are discovered.
notes: Spec reference: TIA-ADAPT-004 — discover SHALL enumerate test items in scope; .venv vendored tests are out of scope. Engine-level exclusion list in run_discover_pipeline (main.rs) also missing .venv.
close_reason: Fixed: added filter_entry to cmd_discover excluding .venv, __pycache__, and 9 other common dirs. Also synced to engine-level run_discover_pipeline. 2 new tests, 108 total pass. PR 6bf2f34.

title: --files flag on discover silently ignored
description:
## Impact

The `--files` flag on `testaruda discover` is accepted by the CLI but has no effect — the discover pipeline always walks the full project tree via `walkdir`.

## Root cause

In `main.rs`, `run_discover_pipeline` assigns the `--files` value to `_delta` (underscore prefix = intentionally unused):

```rust
pub fn run_discover_pipeline(
    store: &testaruda::Store,
    registry: &testaruda::adapter::AdapterRegistry,
    _delta: &testaruda::ChangeSet,  // ← never consulted
) -> std::result::Result<(), String> {
```

## Reproduction

```bash
testaruda discover --files src/main.py
# Still discovers all tests, not just those related to main.py
```

## Location
- `main.rs` — `run_discover_pipeline` function signature
- CLI argument definition for `--files` on discover

## Action
Either:
1. Make `--files` actually scope discovery (pass file paths to adapter's discover, or filter results server-side)
2. Remove the `--files` flag from discover to avoid misleading users

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] `--files` flag either works or is removed from discover help
- [ ] If kept, passing file paths scopes discovery to relevant tests only

## Discovery
Found via testaruda usage report (2026-07-14) — DRAFT-002.
close_reason: Removed --files flag from discover command. Also removed unused _delta parameter from run_discover_pipeline. All 107 tests pass. PR aac041b.

title: bug: beads backlog reports adapter-protocol tickets as closed but core loop still broken
description: testaruda-9uw, testaruda-6js, testaruda-p84, testaruda-gbs are all marked closed with every acceptance criterion checked [x], but the handshake bug (I11) means discover finds 0 test items. The tracker and reality have diverged. Acceptance criteria were verified against unit tests rather than the live CLI path. See docs/evaluations/testaruda-evaluation.md §9.3 (I12)

Live-CLI smoke check (testaruda init && testaruda discover against a real fixture repo) added to acceptance criteria template for adapter-protocol tickets

title: Adapter protocol: static-deps + fingerprint commands
description:
## Phase 2 of adapter protocol

Follow-on from testaruda-9uw (discover flow). Implements:
- `static-deps` command: return candidate tests, K-valued edges, unresolved files (TIA-ADAPT-005)
- Per-symbol edges when `symbol_model_complete` is true
- `fingerprint` command: return content fingerprints at declared granularity (TIA-ADAPT-006)
- Semiring edge values defaulting to multiplicative identity (TIA-ADAPT-009)

Spec: `openspec/specs/adapter-protocol/spec.md`
Contracts: `.espectacular/adapter-protocol/static-dependency-analysis.toml`, `.espectacular/adapter-protocol/content-fingerprinting.toml`, `.espectacular/adapter-protocol/default-semiring-weight.toml`
close_reason: Implemented adapter protocol phase 2: static-deps and fingerprint commands. Added StaticDepsResult/DepEdge/ContentFingerprint types, static_deps() and fingerprint() methods on AdapterIO, store_static_deps() on Store. 6 new tests covering static-deps response, symbol edges, fingerprint response, edge defaults.

title: Implement CI exit codes and shadow mode (TIA-CI-001..008)
description:
Implement correct CI exit codes (0=success, 10=full-run, 20=empty, other=error), shadow mode (compute but report all-tests), machine-readable JSON plan output, and CI result ingestion.

Depends on deterministic ordering (testaruda-x1i) for stable JSON output.

Spec: `openspec/specs/ci-integration/spec.md`
Contracts: `.espectacular/ci-integration/*.toml` (8 contracts)
acceptance_criteria:
- [x] `testaruda select` exits with 0 on success
- [x] Confidence below threshold → exit 10
- [x] Empty selection set → exit 20
- [x] Hard error → non-zero distinct from 10/20
- [x] `--shadow` flag computes selection but signals full run
- [x] `--json` flag emits machine-readable plan
- [x] `testaruda ingest` updates model from CI results
close_reason: Implemented CI exit codes independently of ordering dependency: exit codes 0/10/20, --shadow flag, --json flag, CiPlan output. The JSON output will gain stable ordering when testaruda-x1i is completed.

title: Implement adapter protocol subprocess management (TIA-ADAPT-001..013)
description:
## Phase 1: End-to-end adapter discover flow (this issue)

HITL: Confirm JSON schema for handshake/discover/static-deps commands before implementation (ref: TIA-ADAPT-001 format, spec Appendix C).

Implement the first end-to-end tracer bullet through the adapter protocol:
- Spawn adapter subprocess with least privilege and timeout (TIA-ADAPT-013)
- JSON request/response over stdin/stdout (TIA-ADAPT-001)
- Handshake: parse name, version, protocol, capabilities (TIA-ADAPT-002)
- `discover` command: enumerate test items (TIA-ADAPT-004)
- Store discovered items in the store
- Graceful degradation for missing capabilities (TIA-ADAPT-010)
- Protocol version check (TIA-ADAPT-011)
- Fallback on adapter failure (TIA-ADAPT-012)

Spec: `openspec/specs/adapter-protocol/spec.md`
Contracts: `.espectacular/adapter-protocol/adapter-communication.toml`, `.espectacular/adapter-protocol/handshake-response.toml`, `.espectacular/adapter-protocol/test-discovery.toml`, `.espectacular/adapter-protocol/adapter-sandboxing.toml`, `.espectacular/adapter-protocol/version-mismatch.toml`, `.espectacular/adapter-protocol/adapter-timeout.toml`, `.espectacular/adapter-protocol/missing-capability.toml`
acceptance_criteria:
- [x] Adapter subprocess spawns with timeout and resource limits
- [x] Handshake returns name, version, protocol, capabilities
- [x] Protocol version mismatch → adapter rejected with diagnostic
- [x] Adapter timeout → fallback triggers for component
- [x] Missing capability → core degrades gracefully with conservative default
- [x] `discover` enumerates test items stored in DB
- [x] `cargo test` passes
notes: [2026-07-14] Post-close amendment: added live-CLI smoke check criterion (per I12/tracker-divergence finding). The original "discover enumerates test items stored in DB" was verified only via unit tests — add this criterion to prevent future divergence between test suite and live-CLI behavior.
close_reason: Implemented adapter protocol core: AdapterIO for subprocess management with handshake+discover commands, protocol version check (TIA-ADAPT-011), timeout enforcement (TIA-ADAPT-013), graceful degradation for missing capabilities (TIA-ADAPT-010), AdapterRegistry for extension-to-binary resolution, TestItem types, store_test_items method. 8 new tests covering serialization, deserialization, registry, handshake defaults, discover response, version mismatch detection.

title: Implement content fingerprinting (TIA-CHG-003, TIA-CORE-002)
description:
The store records fingerprints for content units but uses placeholder 'unknown' fingerprints. Implement proper blake3 content fingerprinting for changed-file detection.

- Compute blake3 hash from normalized file content
- Update fingerprint on file changes
- Compare fingerprints to determine change set (TIA-CHG-003)
- Store fingerprint in content_units table (TIA-CORE-002)

Spec: `openspec/specs/change-detection/spec.md`, `openspec/specs/core-data-model/spec.md`
Contracts: `.espectacular/change-detection/fingerprint-comparison.toml`, `.espectacular/core-data-model/fingerprint-storage.toml`
acceptance_criteria:
- [x] `cargo test` passes
- [x] Store records blake3 hash for new content units
- [x] Changed-file detection returns correct Δ for modified files
- [x] Unchanged files produce empty Δ
- [x] Corresponding espectacular contracts transition from no-tests-ran to pass
close_reason: Implemented content fingerprinting: blake3 hash computation in Store::compute_fingerprint, fingerprint comparison in load_selection_context (TIA-CHG-003), cold-start detection (TIA-CHG-009), fingerprint storage (TIA-CORE-002). New tests: test_compute_fingerprint, test_compute_fingerprint_missing_file, test_fingerprint_update_on_selection, test_missing_file_returns_unresolved. Updated fingerprint contracts with targeted test commands.

title: resolve-adapt-014-missing-requirements
description:
GAP: The reworked ADAPT-014 spec in openspec/changes/add-julia-adapter-via-testimonial/specs/adapter-protocol/spec.md includes two scenarios — 'Missing Julia runtime' and 'Missing Testimonial.jl package' — that describe behavior on the testaruda core side (fallback to selecting all tests).

TIA-ADAPT-012 already covers adapter failure fallback: 'If an adapter fails, times out, or returns malformed output, then the core SHALL fall back to selecting all tests in the affected component and record the failure.'

The ADAPT-014 scenarios are therefore redundant with ADAPT-012.

Recommendation: either (a) remove these scenarios from ADAPT-014 since ADAPT-012 already covers adapter startup failure, or (b) add cross-references to ADAPT-012 to avoid duplication. Also check whether ADAPT-012's wording covers the pre-spawn failure case (command not found) or only runtime failures.

title: resolve-testaruda-toml-path-mismatch
description:
POTENTIAL ISSUE: testaruda's testaruda.toml in Testimonial.jl references bin/testaruda_adapter.jl via a relative path: 'julia --project=. bin/testaruda_adapter.jl'. This assumes the adapter is invoked from the Testimonial.jl repo root. But if Testimonial.jl is installed as a system package (via Pkg.add), the bin/ directory won't be at the project root.

The proposal.md says: 'The adapter is opt-in via manual testaruda.toml configuration' and the exact script path is 'to be settled once the install story is clear.'

This ticket tracks: decide on the install-time path resolution strategy. Options:
(a) Document that users must point to the full path of bin/testaruda_adapter.jl
(b) Add a --project flag pointing to the package path
(c) Create a standalone Julia script installable as a global binary
(d) Package the adapter as a separate Julia package

Resolve before the documentation update task (testaruda-k4y).

title: resolve-fingerprint-algorithm-mismatch
description:
MISMATCH: testaruda design.md Decision 2 says BLAKE3 for content fingerprinting ("align to testaruda's own choice"), but Testimonial.jl PROTO-006 says SHA-256 ("to avoid adding a non-standard-library dependency").

Testaruda's ADAPT-006 spec doesn't mandate a specific algorithm — it just says 'return content fingerprints at its declared granularity.' But the design.md explicitly says BLAKE3. This needs a decision: either (a) add SHA-256 as a recognized alternative in the protocol, or (b) add a SHA-256 dependency to Testimonial.jl, or (c) accept SHA-256 in Testimonial.jl and update testaruda's design.md to note that fingerprints are adapter-specific.

Resolution path: since fingerprints are only compared within the same adapter's scope (as PROTO-006 notes), SHA-256 is fine. The fix is to update testaruda's design.md to remove the BLAKE3 requirement for the Julia adapter specifically.
close_reason: Updated design.md (fingerprint row: BLAKE3 → SHA-256), proposal.md (BLAKE3 → SHA-256 with rationale), and tasks.md (1.5 updated). SHA-256 is stdlib in Julia, avoids adding blake3 dep. Fingerprints are only compared within the same adapter's scope per PROTO-006, so algorithm choice is adapter-local.

title: resolve-node-id-format-mismatch
description:
MISMATCH: testaruda ADAPT-015 says node IDs = test_file:line (stable location-based), while Testimonial.jl PROTO-003 says node IDs = test_file:item_name (name-based).

testaruda's spec explicitly calls out the risk:
> Node IDs SHALL be derived from source location (test_file:line) rather than the test-item name, because dynamically-generated names (e.g. @testitem name="test_$i") would produce non-deterministic IDs across invocations.

Testimonial.jl's PROTO-003 says node IDs = test_file:item_name. This is a conflict that must be resolved before the discover command is implemented. Choose one format and update both specs to match.

Resolution options:
(a) Adopt test_file:line per ADAPT-015 and update Testimonial.jl PROTO-003 to match
(b) Adopt test_file:item_name per PROTO-003 and update testaruda ADAPT-015 to match
(c) Introduce a separate stable_id field and use both
close_reason: Resolved: adopted test_file:line (stable location-based) per ADAPT-015. Updated design.md (discover row, run-args row) and tasks.md (1.3). Testimonial.jl PROTO-003 spec updated to match.

title: implement-adapter-run-args

title: implement-adapter-static-deps
description: Implement the static-deps command handler. First invocation (no coverage recorded): return all changed files as unresolved. Subsequent invocations: look up changed files in session_coverage map and return those edges. File-level granularity. Unresolved files trigger TIA-SAFE-004 fallback on the core side.
notes: DEPENDS ON: testaruda-ttp (ingest handler) — static-deps needs the session_coverage map built by ingest.

title: implement-adapter-ingest
description: Implement the ingest command handler. For each item ID in the request: call CoverageLayer.record_item in a subprocess with --code-coverage=user, parse .jl.cov via Coverage.jl, keep count > 0 lines. Return runtime edges (file→line→test). Accumulate results into session_coverage map. No local index persistence. Add espectacular contract for TIA-ADAPT-016 scenarios.
notes:
Note: espectacular contracts for ADAPT-016 are tracked in testaruda-bad. This issue covers only the implementation.
CROSS-REPO DEPENDENCY: Requires testimonial-9yu (.jl.cov sidecar parsing) and testimonial-18p (subprocess command construction) in Testimonial.jl. Also read testaruda-a8c spike findings before implementing — the isolation strategy may change from subprocess-per-item to in-process reset.

title: implement-adapter-handshake
description: Implement the handshake command handler in the Testimonial.jl protocol adapter. Respond with languages=["julia"], granularity="file", capabilities {symbol_model_complete: false, fingerprinting: true, runtime_edges: true}. Add corresponding espectacular contract for TIA-ADAPT-014 scenarios.
notes: Note: espectacular contracts for ADAPT-014 are tracked in testaruda-bad. This issue covers only the implementation.

title: parse_python_imports doesn'\''t handle relative imports
description:
## Impact

The `parse_python_imports` function only handles two patterns at top indentation level:
- `import X` 
- `from X import Y` (absolute imports only)

Not handled:
- `from .module import ...` (relative imports)
- `from ..package import ...`
- Conditional imports inside `try/except`
- Imports inside function bodies
- Dynamic `__import__()` calls

This means the Python adapter misses dependency edges for projects that use relative imports, causing selection to miss real dependencies.

## Location
- `adapter-python.rs` — `parse_python_imports` function

## Action
Use a proper Python import parser (stdlib `ast` module with a Rust binding, or a lightweight regex that handles relative imports) rather than line-based string parsing.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Relative imports (`from .module import ...`) are detected
- [ ] Package-relative imports (`from ..package import ...`) are detected
- [ ] Top-level imports continue to work
- [ ] Test suite passes

## Discovery
Found via testaruda usage report (2026-07-14) — Section 4.
design: Replace line-based string parsing with a solution that handles relative imports (from .module import ...), package-relative imports (from ..package import ...), conditional imports inside try/except, and imports inside function bodies. Approaches include: (a) Rust binding to Python stdlib ast module, (b) lightweight regex that handles dotted relative paths, (c) custom recursive descent parser. The chosen approach must not regress existing absolute import detection.

title: CLI ingest and adapter ingest protocols are disconnected
description:
## Impact

The CLI `ingest` command and the adapter-level `ingest` command are disconnected. The CLI ingest goes directly to `Store::ingest()` and never calls the adapter's ingest. Adapter-level ingest produces `per_test_results` and `runtime_edges`, but there is no path to propagate those into the store's dependency graph.

## Details

- The Python adapter has its own `ingest` command (separate from CLI `testaruda ingest`)
- Adapter ingest accepts `params.run_output` as raw string and parses pytest verbose output for PASSED/FAILED
- Adapter ingest returns `runtime_edges: []` (always empty — `capabilities.runtime_edges: false` in handshake)
- CLI ingest takes a JSON file with `run_id` + `tests` array, calls `Store::ingest()` directly

## Location
- `store.rs` — `Store::ingest()` 
- `adapter-python.rs` — `cmd_ingest`
- `main.rs` — CLI ingest command handler

## Action
Either:
1. (Preferred) Have the CLI ingest delegate to the adapter's ingest and use returned data to populate edges
2. Document the gap clearly and mark adapter-level ingest as deprecated

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] CLI ingest produces runtime dependency edges from test runner output
- [ ] Either ingest path works correctly

## Discovery
Found via testaruda usage report (2026-07-14) — Section 3a.
design: Decision: Deprecate adapter-level ingest protocol and remove it from the adapter contract. The CLI ingest (Store::ingest()) handles all ingestion directly. Adapter-level ingest should return runtime_edges from coverage data. Path forward: (1) Make adapter ingest return coverage-based runtime edges, (2) Have CLI ingest delegate to adapter ingest via run_adapter_pipeline, (3) Feed returned edges into Store::ingest().
acceptance_criteria: Adapter-level ingest returns runtime_edges from parsed coverage output. CLI ingest delegates to adapter ingest before calling Store::ingest(). Runtime edges are persisted in the store. Existing idempotent ingestion behaviour preserved.

title: --agent output lacks node_id and fallback_reason fields
description:
## Impact

The `--agent` output format provides numeric test IDs but no `node_id` (file path), making it hard for agents to map results back to test files without a separate `graph` query. Additionally, when edges are missing (common in v0.1.0), every test shows `always_run: true` with empty `reason_chain`, making it impossible to distinguish "proven affected" from "couldn't prove safe, run everything."

## Details

Current `--agent` output per test:
```json
{ "id": 42, "always_run": true, "reason_chain": [] }
```

Needed:
```json
{ "id": 42, "node_id": "tests/test_model.py", "always_run": true, "fallback_reason": "no edge data available", "reason_chain": [] }
```

## Location
- `main.rs` — agent output format generation

## Action
Add `node_id` (file path) and `fallback_reason` (why test is in always_run state) to agent output.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] `--agent` output includes `node_id` for each test
- [ ] `--agent` output includes `fallback_reason` explaining always_run state
- [ ] Output remains parseable as JSON

## Discovery
Found via testaruda usage report (2026-07-14) — Section 5.
notes: Spec reference: openspec change add-agent-output-fields (MODIFIES TIA-AGENT-001). This change adds node_id and fallback_reason per-test fields to the agent output format.

title: Configurable discover exclusion list in testaruda.toml
description:
## Impact

## Action

Add a `[discover]` section to `testaruda.toml` with an `exclude` list. The adapter discover walk and engine-level pipeline SHALL skip directories matching any pattern in the list.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] testaruda.toml supports [discover] section with exclude list
- [ ] Discover walk skips all directories matching exclude patterns
- [ ] Engine-level pipeline also applies exclude patterns
- [ ] Default exclude list matches common patterns from testaruda-6j0
- [ ] User can extend or replace default exclude patterns

## Discovery
Split from testaruda-6j0 during issue-review pass. testaruda-6j0 is the hardcoded bug fix (P1); this is the configurable follow-up (P3 feature).

title: init should auto-detect project language
description:
## Impact

On a Python-only project, `testaruda discover` runs the default (Rust) adapter and finds 0 tests. The user must manually edit `testaruda.toml` to change `default = "testaruda-adapter-python"`.

This creates a poor first-run experience and requires reading docs to discover the workaround.

## Suggested approach

Have `init` auto-detect the project language (check for `pyproject.toml` vs `Cargo.toml`), or default to the first configured adapter alphabetically rather than hard-coding `testaruda-adapter-rust`.

## Location
- `main.rs` — `init` command handler
- Config generation in `store.rs` or CLI

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] `init` detects Python projects (presence of `pyproject.toml`, `setup.py`, `setup.cfg`)
- [ ] `init` detects Rust projects (presence of `Cargo.toml`)
- [ ] Default adapter matches detected language
- [ ] Works for mixed-language projects

## Discovery
Found via testaruda usage report (2026-07-14) — Section 1.
notes: Spec reference: openspec change add-init-language-detection (ADDS TIA-CHG-009). Specifies init-time probing for pyproject.toml, Cargo.toml, etc. to determine default adapter.

title: --json and --pre-edit flags conflict silently
description:
## Impact

The `--json` and `--pre-edit` flags on `select` cannot be combined, but the CLI doesn't validate this. Using both produces confusing/invalid output instead of a clear error message.

## Location
- `main.rs` — CLI argument handling for `select` command

## Action
Add mutual exclusion validation between `--json` and `--pre-edit` flags. Return a clear error message if both are provided.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Using `--json` and `--pre-edit` together produces an error message
- [ ] Each flag works independently
- [ ] Help text mentions mutual exclusivity

## Discovery
Found via testaruda usage report (2026-07-14) — Section 5.

title: Predictive ranking for test ordering (TIA-SEL-007, TIA-VER-005)
description:
## Requirements

TIA-SEL-007 from `openspec/specs/selection-engine/spec.md` and TIA-VER-005 from `openspec/specs/verification/spec.md`:

- **SEL-007** — Predictive ranking: order selected tests by predicted failure likelihood
- **VER-005** — Ranking calibration gate: hold-out evaluation before promoting ranking model

Currently only deterministic (test ID) and duration-based ordering are implemented (SEL-005, SEL-006).

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Predictive ranking model interface defined
- [ ] Training data collected from run history
- [ ] Basic frequency-based ranking (order by historical failure rate)
- [ ] Calibration gate with recall targets
notes: Implemented: TestOrdering::Predictive, load_failure_rates(), frequency-based ranking, test coverage. Calibration gate (VER-005) deferred to separate ticket.

title: CI result ingestion (TIA-CI-008)
description:
## Requirements

TIA-CI-008 from `openspec/specs/ci-integration/spec.md`:

- **CI-008** — Result ingestion: CI mode automatically ingests test results after running selected tests

Currently, `testaruda ingest` is a separate manual step. CI-008 would make it automatic after the test run.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] `testaruda select --ci` optionally runs tests and ingests results
- [ ] Test runner output is captured and fed to ingest automatically
- [ ] Exit codes reflect post-ingestion state

title: Flaky test detection and exclusion (TIA-SAFE-011, TIA-SAFE-012)
description:
## Requirements

TIA-SAFE-011 and TIA-SAFE-012 from `openspec/specs/safety/spec.md`:

- **SAFE-011** — Flaky detection: identify tests whose outcomes oscillate between passed/failed across runs on the same selection
- **SAFE-012** — Flaky exclusion from training: exclude flaky test outcomes from confidence scoring

The store schema already accepts `flaky` as an outcome value — detection logic is what's missing.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Flaky detection heuristic implemented (e.g., N retries, outcome oscillation tracking)
- [ ] Flaky tests excluded from confidence model
- [ ] Flaky status surfaced in agent output and explain

title: Observability: metrics emission and structured logs (TIA-OBS-003, TIA-OBS-004)
description:
## Requirements

TIA-OBS-003 and TIA-OBS-004 from `openspec/specs/observability/spec.md`:

- **OBS-003** — Metrics emission: emit counters and histograms for selection latency, test counts, confidence distribution
- **OBS-004** — Structured logs: machine-parseable log output with consistent fields

OBS-001 (graph export) and OBS-002 (selection explanation) are already implemented.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Basic metrics emitted during selection (counts, latency)
- [ ] Structured log output with JSON format
- [ ] Configurable log level

title: Local mode: daemon, watch, rerun (TIA-LOCAL-001..005)
description:
## Requirements

TIA-LOCAL-001..005 from `openspec/specs/local-mode/spec.md`:

- **LOCAL-001** — Working tree selection: `select` uses the local working tree as change source when no base/head revisions are given
- **LOCAL-002** — Daemon mode: background process that caches state across invocations
- **LOCAL-003** — Watch mode: file-system watcher that re-runs selection on change
- **LOCAL-004** — Local failure rerun: re-run only failed tests from last local run
- **LOCAL-005** — Offline operation: no external dependencies required

## Dependencies

Depends on core selection pipeline (implemented in v0.2.0).

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] `testaruda select` with no args works on working tree
- [ ] Daemon mode specification written
- [ ] Watch mode specification written
- [ ] Design doc for local workflow

title: chore: remove unused dependencies from Cargo.toml
description: similar, uuid, rayon, ascent-byods-rels, and serde_yaml are declared in Cargo.toml but referenced nowhere in src/. Originally reported as I8. Only blake3 and toml have been wired in. See docs/evaluations/testaruda-evaluation.md §9.1
acceptance_criteria: Each of similar, uuid, rayon, ascent-byods-rels, serde_yaml is either used in src/ or removed from Cargo.toml
close_reason: Removed 5 unused deps from Cargo.toml: similar, uuid, rayon, ascent-byods-rels, serde_yaml. Build and all 97 tests pass.

title: fix: justfile parse error (I6 regression)
notes:
The justfile had a Markdown/HTML boilerplate block prepended above the real recipes, preventing just from parsing it. This blocked all just recipes including `just test`, `just build`, `just check`, and `just ah`.

Root cause: Markdown fenced code blocks and HTML comments accidentally committed into the recipe file.

Fix applied (https://github.com/charly/testaruda/commit/WIP): Replaced the Markdown preamble with 16 proper just recipes and removed all non-just content.

Verification:
- `just --list` shows 16 available recipes
- `just build` compiles successfully

Closes: I6 from the testaruda evaluation, and Backlog gap B (§8.4).
close_reason: Fixed: replaced Markdown preamble with proper justfile recipes. 16 recipes available, just build passes.

title: Implement missed-selection incident recording (TIA-SAFE-008)
description:
When a full run fails a test that selection would have skipped, record a missed-selection incident and create a manual edge forcing the test on the implicated change in future.

Spec: `openspec/specs/safety/spec.md`
Contracts: `.espectacular/safety/missed-selection-recording.toml`
acceptance_criteria:
- [x] Full run failure that selection skipped → incident recorded
- [x] Manual edge created forcing the test on the implicated change
- [x] Missed-selection count exposed via metrics (TIA-OBS-003)
- [x] `cargo test` passes

title: Implement user-defined must-run rules and periodic full-run (TIA-SAFE-006, TIA-SAFE-009)
description:
Implement config-driven forced selection rules covering two mechanisms:
1. Must-run rules (TIA-SAFE-009): path globs mapped to tests, force-select when matching files change.
2. Periodic full-run (TIA-SAFE-006): configurable schedule independent of change-based selection.

Spec: `openspec/specs/safety/spec.md`
Contracts: `.espectacular/safety/must-run-pattern-match.toml`, `.espectacular/safety/periodic-full-run-configured.toml`
acceptance_criteria:
- [x] Must-run glob patterns force-select mapped tests on matching file changes
- [x] Periodic full-run schedule selects all tests regardless of changes
- [x] Configuration in `testaruda.toml` or equivalent
- [x] `cargo test` passes

title: Implement Soufflé oracle bridge (TIA-ENG-010, TIA-ENG-011)
description:
HITL: Confirm JSON schema for handshake/discover commands before implementation.

Phase 1: Wire existing `Command::Validate` stub (src/main.rs:71-79) to find souffle binary on PATH.
Phase 2: Implement shadow-mode cross-check against Ascent results (TIA-ENG-011).

Requires `souffle` CLI on PATH for verification. On `testaruda init` detect presence and warn if missing.

Spec: `openspec/specs/engine/spec.md`
Contracts: `.espectacular/engine/soufflé-validation.toml`, `.espectacular/engine/shadow-mode-divergence-detection.toml`
acceptance_criteria:
- [x] `testaruda oracle` finds souffle binary and executes Datalog program
- [x] Shadow mode cross-check flags Ascent/Soufflé divergences
- [x] `init` warns if souffle not found without failing

title: Implement environment fingerprinting (TIA-CORE-008, TIA-RUN-006)
description:
Partition edges and statistics by environment fingerprint. Record environment on ingestion. Support environment-scoped queries.

Runs in parallel with most other issues.

Spec: `openspec/specs/core-data-model/spec.md`, `openspec/specs/runtime-feedback/spec.md`
Contracts: `.espectacular/core-data-model/environment-scoped-queries.toml`, `.espectacular/runtime-feedback/environment-fingerprint-on-ingest.toml`

title: Implement graph export/import (TIA-STORE-003)
description:
Complete the graph export/import mechanism: documented interchange format for dependency graph and provenance, supporting both export and import commands.

Runs in parallel with most other issues.

Spec: `openspec/specs/persistence/spec.md`
Contracts: `.espectacular/persistence/graph-export.toml`

title: Respect NO_COLOR and disable ANSI escapes on non-TTY output (UX9)
description:
Round 5 UX9 (papercut): ANSI color escapes are emitted unconditionally even when stdout/stderr is piped to a file or non-TTY. Compounds UX1 in that redirecting output is also unsafe without RUST_LOG=off or NO_COLOR support.

Recommendation: Configure tracing_subscriber to respect NO_COLOR env var and disable colors when output is not a TTY. Can be bundled with the UX1/OBS-005 fix since both are tracing_subscriber config changes.

title: Add shell completions subcommand (clap_complete) (UX8)
description:
Round 5 UX8 (papercut): No testaruda completions <shell> subcommand exists. clap_complete makes this close to a one-function addition for a clap-based CLI. Every flag becomes tab-discoverable instead of requiring --help.

Recommendation: Add 'testaruda completions bash|zsh|fish|powershell' using clap_complete.

title: Collapse duplicate quick-start docs into one canonical Tutorial (UX7)
description:
Round 5 UX7 (papercut): README.md Quick Start and docs/getting-started.md First Run are near-identical command sequences. Both also restate reference content (exit-code table, adapter-config TOML snippet) that already lives in dedicated reference docs.

Recommendation: Collapse to one Tutorial (getting-started.md, commands + expected output only) that links to cli.md/configuration.md for detail rather than restating it.

title: Fix explain command: distinguish 'no dependencies' from 'unknown test id' (UX10)
description:
Round 5 UX10 (papercut): testaruda explain 9999 returns {dependencies: [], test_id: 9999} with exit 0 — identical to a real test that happens to have zero dependencies. A developer investigating 'why wasn't my test selected' gets no signal they typo'd the ID.

Recommendation: explain SHALL return a non-zero exit code and an error message when the requested test_id does not exist.

title: Engine scale-up: DBSP, migration, store independence (TIA-ENG-013..016)
description:
## Requirements

TIA-ENG-013..016 from `openspec/specs/engine/spec.md`:

- **ENG-013** — DBSP scale-up path: alternative engine backend for large-scale workloads
- **ENG-014** — Engine migration path: mechanism to switch between engines
- **ENG-015** — Store independence: engine operates on store data without file-system coupling
- **ENG-016** — Memory safety and subprocess isolation: sandboxed engine execution

These are aspirational/long-term — not needed for v1.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] DBSP integration design document
- [ ] Engine trait/interface defined
- [ ] Store independence proof-of-concept

title: Composability: multi-repo, remote cache, shard plan (TIA-COMP-005..012)
description:
## Requirements

TIA-COMP-005..012 from `openspec/specs/composability/spec.md`:

- **COMP-005** — Cross-repo edge recording
- **COMP-006** — Interface change propagation
- **COMP-007** — Aggregation without global lock
- **COMP-008** — Parallel per-component selection
- **COMP-009** — Order-independent results
- **COMP-010** — Cached selection decisions
- **COMP-011** — Remote cache
- **COMP-012** — Shard plan

COMP-001..004 (component graph, inter-component edges, bottom-up resolution, multi-repo manifest) are foundational and may need to come first.

## Dependencies

Requires COMP-001..004 as foundation. This is a major distributed-systems feature set.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Design document for multi-repo architecture
- [ ] Cross-repo edge format specified
- [ ] Remote cache protocol designed
- [ ] Shard plan format designed

title: I6 (retrospective): fix justfile parsing
description:
## Background

I6 from the evaluation: the justfile had Markdown prose and a fenced code block prepended above the real recipes, causing `just` to fail with:

> error: unknown start of token '<'  ——▶ justfile:36:1

Every recipe (`just test`, `just build`, `just check`, `just ah`) was unusable. Originally reported in docs/evaluations/testaruda-evaluation.md §3 (I6).

## Status

Already fixed in implementation — confirmed "✅ fixed" in evaluation §9.1. This is a retrospective ticket for beads tracking completeness.

## Acceptance criteria
- [x] `just --list` succeeds and lists all 16 recipes
